items.prompt: Tap the nodes a search for 38 visits, from the root down.
hints: Find where 38 fits among the root's keys.
20 < 38 < 40, so go to the middle child, where 38 is.

items.prompt: Tap the nodes a search for 55 visits, from the root down. (55 may not be in the tree.)
hints: 55 is larger than the last key, 40.
Go right to [50 | 60]. It is a leaf without 55, so the search stops there.

items.prompt: You search this tree for 45. What happens?
hints: Where does 45 fit among the root's keys?
Follow the child for that range; stop at a leaf.
45 > 40 → last child [50 | 60]. It is a leaf and 45 is not in it, so 45 is not in the tree.

options.text: It goes to [50 | 60], a leaf, and reports that 45 is not in the tree
options.feedback: Right. Reaching a leaf without the key means it is not there.

options.text: It goes to the middle child, because 45 is close to 40
options.feedback: Searches follow ranges, not nearness. 45 > 40, so the last child.

options.text: It stops at the root, because 45 is not there
options.feedback: A key can be in any node below. Only a leaf without the key ends the search.

items.prompt: A B-tree is 3 levels tall. At most, how many nodes does a search visit?
hints: A search moves down one level at a time.
It visits one node per level.

options.feedback: Each comparison rules out all but one child, so most nodes are skipped.
The order limits keys per node, not nodes visited.
